headline: Microsoft surged last night on strong AI revenue outlook while the ASX held steady today — Gold Coast winter skies clear and calm at 17.9°C.

portfolio.summary: Your US holdings were the main movers last night. Microsoft jumped over 2% after bullish analyst coverage, while Google slipped about 1%. On the ASX today, everything was pretty quiet — your ETFs barely budged, with the emerging markets ETF (VGE) the standout, up 0.7%.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Jumped last night after Morgan Stanley flagged strong AI revenue momentum and Morningstar put a $600 price target on the stock — currently trading at $460.52 USD, so there's implied upside of ~30% in their view.

movers.name: Alphabet (Google)
movers.note: Slipped last night with no major news catalyst — likely some rotation out of Google and into Microsoft as AI coding competition heats up. Down $3.97 to $376.37 USD.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Edged higher last night, riding continued GTA 6 hype. Take-Two's CEO was out saying GTA's success bar is extraordinarily high, even for ex-Rockstar staff — which markets seem to like as a sign of quality control.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: Best ASX performer in your portfolio today, up 0.7% to $93.65. Emerging markets getting a small lift, possibly from a steady Aussie dollar and softer oil prices.

movers.name: BetaShares Global Energy ETF
movers.note: Nudged up slightly today despite oil (WTI crude) dropping 1.3% last night to $90.93 USD. The ETF held its ground — up 3 cents to $8.55.

movers.name: Commonwealth Bank
movers.note: Barely moved today, down 30 cents to $163.00. No major CBA-specific news — broader ASX 200 was also flat, off just 0.06%.

markets.summary: Last night in the US, the S&P 500 and NASDAQ both ticked higher — the NASDAQ up 0.42% and the S&P up 0.26% — largely driven by tech and AI enthusiasm. Gold had a big night, surging nearly 2% to $4,561 USD/oz. Oil dropped 1.3% to $90.93. The Aussie dollar was essentially flat at 71.85 US cents. Locally, the ASX 200 closed basically unchanged today, down just 5 points to 8,724.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Flat close today — nothing dramatic on the ASX.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Modest gain last night, tech leading.

indicators.name: NASDAQ Composite
indicators.note: Tech stocks lifted the NASDAQ last night.

indicators.name: Gold (USD/oz)
indicators.note: Big move higher last night — gold near record highs, investors seeking safety.

indicators.name: Crude Oil WTI (USD/barrel)
indicators.note: Oil fell last night, easing some pressure on energy costs.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: Aussie dollar barely moved — steady at about 71.85 US cents.

politics.summary: Two big RBA-related stories dominated Australian political and economic news today — the housing market is feeling the pinch from high interest rates, and an RBA board member flagged that inflation is still stubborn. Meanwhile, Labor is rushing contentious tax reform through parliament with almost no scrutiny time.

stories.title: RBA and Chalmers point to interest rates and taxes as culprits for falling house prices
stories.why_it_matters: Both the RBA and Treasurer Jim Chalmers are acknowledging that high interest rates and the tax treatment of property are contributing to softer house prices. This is a notable shift — the government is essentially conceding that policy settings are cooling the market. For property owners and investors, it signals the pressure isn't going away soon, and any changes to negative gearing or CGT (capital gains tax — the discount you get when selling an asset) could add further headwinds to property values.

stories.title: RBA's Harper warns inflation persistence remains a significant issue
stories.why_it_matters: RBA board member Ian Harper said today that inflation staying high is still a 'significant issue' for the central bank. In plain English: the RBA isn't done worrying about prices, and rate cuts aren't on the near-term horizon. This keeps pressure on mortgage holders and means borrowing costs stay elevated for longer — not great news if you were hoping rates would drop soon.

stories.title: Labor gives parliament just two days to scrutinise CGT and negative gearing changes
stories.why_it_matters: Labor is fast-tracking proposed changes to CGT (capital gains tax — the tax you pay when you sell an investment at a profit) and negative gearing (where you deduct rental property losses against your income) through parliament with only two days for scrutiny. Critics say this is nowhere near enough time to examine changes that could significantly affect property investors. If you own investment properties or assets like shares, these reforms could directly affect how much tax you pay when you sell. The rush is drawing serious criticism from the opposition and industry groups.

ai.summary: The big AI story today is the race between Microsoft and Google to dominate AI-powered coding tools — analysts say it's a massive growth battleground. There's also growing concern about the patchwork of AI regulations popping up across different countries and US states, with no consistent rulebook emerging yet.

stories.title: Microsoft and Google racing to lead AI coding — analysts say it's 'absolutely critical' for growth
stories.why_it_matters: Analysts are calling AI coding tools — software that writes, checks, and fixes code for developers — the next massive revenue frontier for both Microsoft (GitHub Copilot) and Google (Gemini Code Assist). Both companies are playing catch-up to specialised startups, but their scale means they could dominate if they get it right. For you as a MSFT and GOOGL holder, this is the key growth battleground to watch — whoever wins the developer market wins recurring enterprise revenue for years.

stories.title: New national index tracks the growing patchwork of AI healthcare regulations
stories.why_it_matters: A new index is being built in the US to track how AI is being regulated in healthcare across different states — because there's currently no single national rulebook, just a messy patchwork of local laws. For AI companies like Google (which has major healthcare AI projects) and Microsoft (Azure health cloud), this regulatory fragmentation adds compliance cost and uncertainty. Worth watching as a long-term risk for your US tech holdings.

stories.title: Trump cheerleads for AI, but some in MAGA world are nervous
stories.why_it_matters: While Trump is loudly backing AI development in the US, some of his own supporters are worried about job losses and the social disruption that comes with rapid automation. This tension inside the Republican base could affect future US AI policy — particularly around regulation and worker protections. For now it's background noise, but it's a reminder that US AI policy isn't a settled bipartisan love story.

sport.summary: NRL Round 14 team lists are out with the Warriors on a bye. The big Rugby storyline is the Chiefs landing another marquee signing. In AFL, there's a widening gap between the top teams and the rest of the competition, and James Hird is back in the news.

stories.title: NRL Round 14 team lists confirmed — Warriors on bye
stories.why_it_matters: All Round 14 squads are confirmed with kick-off starting Thursday night — Sea Eagles vs Rabbitohs at 4 Pines Park. The Warriors are sitting this round out on a bye. The Queensland local derby — Broncos vs Titans at Suncorp on Saturday night at 7:35 PM — is the pick of the weekend for Gold Coast fans.

stories.title: Perth Bears poaching top Queensland NRL prospects ahead of 2027 debut
stories.why_it_matters: The incoming Perth Bears NRL franchise (joining in 2027) are aggressively recruiting and are on the verge of signing a top Queensland prospect, according to CODE Sports. The Bears have also been busy locking in a broader squad — CODE published a full rundown of their signings so far and a projected best 17. Queensland clubs will need to start tightening their retention contracts or risk losing more local talent west.

stories.title: Chiefs land another star signing in Super Rugby
stories.why_it_matters: The Waikato Chiefs have pulled off another surprise signing ahead of the Super Rugby Pacific finals. No article text was available with specific player details, but the move reinforces the Chiefs' status as the dominant force in this year's competition and a likely title favourite.

stories.title: AFL top tier creating daylight over the rest — NFL-style nightmare scenario now possible
stories.why_it_matters: Fox Sports analysis today argues there is now a massive and growing gap between AFL's elite clubs and the rest of the competition — and that it's starting to resemble American NFL-style inequality where a handful of powerhouse teams dominate year after year. The piece raises the concern that if the AFL doesn't act on the talent and financial imbalances, finals football becomes predictable and fan interest in weaker clubs could fade. No specific clubs are named in the available data, but the piece flags it as a structural problem for the competition.

watch_today.title: MSFT: Strong analyst tailwinds — hold and watch for further upside
watch_today.detail: Last night's 2.28% gain was backed by real substance — Morgan Stanley flagged strong AI revenue momentum and Morningstar put a $600 price target on it (it's currently at $460.52, implying ~30% upside in their model). No reason to sell into strength here. The AI coding race story from CNBC also directly benefits Microsoft's GitHub Copilot product. Hold comfortably.

watch_today.title: CGT and negative gearing reform: watch for property/tax impacts this week
watch_today.detail: Labor is pushing CGT and negative gearing changes through parliament with only two days of scrutiny. If you hold investment properties or plan to sell any assets, it's worth understanding what's changing. The reforms could reduce the CGT discount (currently 50% of your profit is tax-free after 12 months) and tighten negative gearing on existing properties. Watch for the final legislation details this week.

watch_today.title: Oil dropping — mild headwind for FUEL.AX this week
watch_today.detail: Crude oil fell 1.33% last night to $90.93 USD per barrel. FUEL.AX held up okay today (+0.35%) but if oil keeps sliding that'll weigh on your energy ETF. No action needed yet — just keep an eye on oil prices as the week progresses.

watch_today.title: Gold surging — not a direct holding but worth knowing
watch_today.detail: Gold jumped nearly 2% last night to $4,561 USD/oz, near record highs. This usually signals investors are nervous about something — could be geopolitical tension (Iran-US, Israel-Lebanon conflict was cited in energy news) or inflation fears. Your VDHG and VTS ETFs have some indirect exposure to gold miners. More of a macro 'vibe check' than an action item.

watch_today.title: RBA rate cut hopes fading — CBA.AX may face pressure
watch_today.detail: RBA board member Harper's comments today that inflation persistence is a 'significant issue' push back on any near-term rate cut hopes. Bank stocks like CBA generally do fine in a high-rate environment on net interest margins, but sentiment can soften if the economy slows. CBA barely moved today. Hold — no new catalyst either way.
